title: Monthly Disability Compensation in a Veterans Pension Benefit Income Statement
content:
Compensation paid to a Veterans Pension recipient counts as income for pension only for months before pension was first paid; compensation paid for a month that pension also paid is settled against the pension for that month and is not counted as income.

## Rule for the monthly compensation in a benefit income statement

The monthly VA disability compensation stated in the veteran's benefit income statement depends on the veteran's Disability Compensation award — its status and the reason it ended — and on the monthly compensation payments in its payment ledger issued since the pension effective date:

1. When the Disability Compensation award ended by the veteran's election of pension and monthly compensation was issued since the pension effective date, no monthly compensation is stated, because every month it paid was also a month of pension.
2. When the Disability Compensation award is still running and monthly compensation was issued in that period, the most recent monthly payment is stated for 12 months.
3. In every other case the monthly compensation issued in that period is stated as issued — the total of those payments.

## Combinations

| Award ended by election of pension | Award running | Monthly compensation issued since the pension effective date | Monthly compensation stated |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | — | Yes | 0 |
| — | Yes | Yes | most recent monthly payment, for 12 months |
| Yes | — | No | total issued (0) |
| — | Yes | No | total issued (0) |
| No, ended for another reason | — | Yes or No | total issued in the period |

## Worked figures (hypothetical ledger: monthly payments of 1100.00, 1100.00 and 1150.00 issued since the pension effective date)

- Award ended by election of pension: 0.
- Award running: 1150.00 for 12 months, which is 13800.00.
- Award ended for any other reason: 1100.00 plus 1100.00 plus 1150.00, which is 3350.00.
